# authentik-laravel

> Single sign-on against authentik for Laravel. One group per application is the
> entire access model. Roles are never derived from authentik.

## What this package does

Adds authentik sign-in (OIDC authorization code + PKCE) to a Laravel application,
and decides whether the signed-in user may use the application at all. It does not
manage roles, permissions or users.

## The access rule, in full

1. Create one group per application in authentik, e.g. `myapp-access`.
2. If the signed-in user's group list contains that group, they may use the app.
3. Otherwise they are denied.
4. Roles are the application's own concern and must not be set from authentik.

## Install

```json
{
  "repositories": [
    { "type": "vcs", "url": "https://github.com/rmachhh/authentik-laravel" }
  ],
  "require": {
    "rmachhh/authentik-laravel": "0.2.4"
  }
}
```

```bash
composer update rmachhh/authentik-laravel
php artisan vendor:publish --tag=authentik-config
```

Requires PHP 8.1+ and Laravel 10, 11, 12 or 13. No runtime dependency beyond the
framework: HTTP goes through Laravel's client, so `Http::fake()` works in tests.

## Minimal integration

`SETUP.md` in this repository contains the complete, exact code to add. Follow it
literally rather than inventing the wiring.

The shape, for orientation:

```php
// 1. start
$result = Authentik::startAuthorization();          // ['url' => ..., 'flow' => ...]
Session::put('authentik.flow', $result['flow']->toArray());
return redirect()->away($result['url']);

// 2. finish
$flow = FlowState::fromArray(Session::pull('authentik.flow', []));
$remote = Authentik::completeLogin(request()->query(), $flow);
abort_unless($remote->hasAccessTo(config('authentik.app_group')), 403);

// 3. protect
Route::middleware(['web', 'authentik.group'])->group(...);
```

## Required environment

| Variable | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `AUTHENTIK_ISSUER` | `https://id.example.com/application/o/myapp/` | Trailing slash matters |
| `AUTHENTIK_CLIENT_ID` | `myapp` | From the provider |
| `AUTHENTIK_CLIENT_SECRET` | | Server-side only |
| `AUTHENTIK_REDIRECT_URI` | `https://myapp.example.com/auth/authentik/callback` | Must match the provider exactly |
| `AUTHENTIK_APP_GROUP` | `myapp-access` | The group that grants access |
| `AUTHENTIK_APP_ROLE` | `superadmin` | Optional. Only for a system with one role. |

## API

| Member | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `Authentik::startAuthorization()` | Build the PKCE URL and the flow state to store |
| `Authentik::completeLogin($query, $flow)` | Validate state, PKCE and nonce; return an `AuthentikUser` |
| `AuthentikUser::hasAccessTo($group)` | The access decision; fails closed |
| `AuthentikUser::matchedGroup($group)` | Which group granted access, for logging |
| `AuthentikUser::hasVerifiedEmail()` | True only when the provider asserts the address is verified |
| `authentik.group` middleware | 403 when the group is missing, redirect when not signed in |
| `Authentik::instances()` | Configured instances, in the order tried |
| `AuthentikUserImport::recoveryLink($email)` | Single-use password-set link; `null` when no account exists |
| `AuthentikUserImport::groupMembers()` | The access group's members with `pk`/`username`/`email`; one request |
| `AuthentikUserImport::deleteUser($pk)` | Delete one identity; `false` when it was already gone |

## Failover

Configure several instances in `config/authentik.php`. The first reachable one
starts a sign-in. The callback completes against the instance that started it,
because a code can only be exchanged by its issuer. Configuration errors are not
failed over.

## Importing users

`AuthentikUserImport` moves an application's users into authentik. It is
repeatable: an existing user is not recreated, and membership is only written
when missing. It never deletes anyone, never sets a password, and never mirrors
roles. Call `preview($users)` first — it writes nothing.

Needs `AUTHENTIK_ADMIN_URL` and `AUTHENTIK_ADMIN_TOKEN`, separate from the
sign-in credentials because the token is far more powerful.

## Rules an agent must not break

- Never assign roles or permissions from the groups claim.
- Never treat an empty group list as "no access" when the user already has local
  roles; leave existing access alone.
- Never log tokens, codes or client secrets.
- Never default the app group to something permissive. No group configured means
  deny everything.
- Never send the PKCE verifier, state or nonce to the browser in readable form.
- Do not allow `allow_insecure` outside local development.
- Never match a local account on an email address unless
  `AuthentikUser::hasVerifiedEmail()` is true.
- Never relink an account whose `authentik_sub` is already set to a different
  value.
- Never assume an imported user can sign in. A new identity has an unusable
  password and needs a recovery link before its owner can authenticate.

## Verifying the work

1. `php artisan authentik:doctor` — checks configuration, discovery, PKCE, the
   redirect URI and the access guard, and prints a fix for each failure.
2. `vendor/bin/phpunit` — the package suite.
3. `php tests/live-check.php` — the same checks plus failover, against a running
   authentik.

## Documentation

- `SETUP.md` — the exact code to add, with a verification step
- `README.md` — full API reference
